summary: PASS — Universal Highlightly rollout + game-centered highlights verified end-to-end (backend + frontend web). BACKEND: 5/5 pytest cases green in /app/backend/tests/test_highlightly.py: (a) GET /api/highlights?league=nhl&limit=5 returns {league:'nhl', clips:[...]} with each clip carrying youtube_id, thumbnail, title, category, date, home, away; (b) GET /api/highlights?league=ahl&limit=3 returns real AHL clips (Calder Cup window active) with correct shape and limit obeyed; (c) GET /api/highlights/match?league=nhl&home=Vegas Golden Knights&away=Carolina Hurricanes&date=2026-06-15T00:00:00Z returns recap.youtube_id == '3jbQ58HKtXA' (Cup Final Game 6); (d) GET /api/highlights/match with nonsense teams (home=Zzz&away=Qqq) returns {recap:null, clips:[]} — graceful, no fabrication, HTTP 200; (e) GET /api/leagues exposes capabilities.video on every league and both nhl AND whl are True. Total pytest wall time 1.92s. FRONTEND: On mobile viewport 390x844, navigated directly to /game/2025030416 (NHL Cup Final Game 6 — CAR beat VGK 3-0, series 4-2). The HIGHLIGHTS section with testID 'highlights-module' rendered ABOVE the 'GAME DESK' Reggie+Marc panel (bounding-rect check: hmTop=307 < deskTop=767). The recap hero (testID 'highlight-hero') showed the 16:9 Highlightly thumbnail with play-circle overlay, 'GAME RECAP' badge (blue accent), the clip title 'Hurricanes vs. Golden Knights | NHL Playoff Highlights | Game 6 | June 14, 2026', 'via NHL' channel line, and the 'Verified video · Highlightly' credit exactly once. Tapping the hero on web triggered Linking.openURL against the verified YouTube source URL and did NOT crash the web bundle (module still mounted, body content unchanged, 0 pageerrors, 0 console errors). The web-safe YoutubeInline.web.tsx correctly isolates react-native-youtube-iframe from the web build (renders an empty View, never imports the native player). The empty-package path is guaranteed by code (HighlightsModule returns null when !pkg.recap) and is corroborated by the backend nonsense-teams test returning recap:null. No deprecated Expo packages, no SafeAreaView issues, no text-outside-Text issues detected in the touched files.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/highlightly.py: clean, small, additive adapter. Key is read lazily via _key() so load_dotenv timing is not an issue. In-memory _CACHE keyed by (leagueId, limit) with 15-min TTL is appropriate for the 7500 calls/day Pro-plan budget. On fetch failure it falls back to the last-good cache entry, which is the right behavior. HL_LEAGUES is a single plug point per the design intent — adding a league is one line.

match_highlights() correctly uses BOTH team nicknames + date-proximity (diff<=2 days) for playoff-series disambiguation, and clips are sorted by date proximity so the closest match becomes the recap. Returns {recap:None, clips:[]} on empty nicknames or no match — no fabrication.

server.py /api/highlights and /api/highlights/match both wrap the adapter in try/except and always return a well-shaped payload so the client can render nothing safely; /api/leagues correctly OR-merges provider media capability with highlightly.covers(code) so video=true for any Highlightly-covered league even if the provider doesn't natively expose media.

HighlightsModule.tsx: module-level `cache` object keyed by `${league}:${away}@${home}:${date}` makes re-opening a game instant with zero extra API calls. Early-return `if (!pkg || !pkg.recap) return null` guarantees NO empty box when nothing matches — matches the 'never a placeholder' rule. Platform.OS==='web' branch calls Linking.openURL(clip.url) and skips the Modal path entirely, which is why the react-native-youtube-iframe web-bundle issue is neutralised.
YoutubeInline.web.tsx: correctly no-op View so the web bundle never imports react-native-youtube-iframe. Metro's platform-specific resolution (.web.tsx) is the right isolation mechanism here.
